Of this fire, **Phiares** <note>A name often appearing in medieval alchemical compendiums</note> the philosopher says: The property of the fire of the **horse's belly** <note>original: "Roßbauchs"; a metaphorical term for the warm, moist environment of a digestion vessel</note> is that it does not destroy the **gold**, but rather increases it through its moisture, whereas other fires destroy it through their dryness. That quicksilver is [our fire]
</margin>

# DICTA <note>Latin for "Sayings" or "Dictates," referring to the authoritative teachings of alchemical masters.</note>

...may become a growth and increase without end, and therefore the **transformation** of things is now sufficiently known and manifest, with every possibility, according to what the **Philosophers** <note>In alchemical texts, "Philosophers" refers to the historical masters of the "Hermetic Art," such as Hermes Trismegistus, Geber, or Arnald of Villanova.</note> say.

Whoever can or knows how to **break** <note>original: "erbrechen"; here meaning to decompose or "open" the metallic structure to return it to its liquid or "primordial" state</note> gold or silver, so that it is henceforth no longer gold, he attains a great **Mastery**. For it is common knowledge that we see copper take on a gold color and become **Brass**; from lead we make **White Lead** and **Minium** <note>original: "Mening"; red lead oxide, used as a pigment and in glass-making</note>, and from minium a **Glass**; yet it always remains as it was, and each thing stays in its own untransformed essence. Thus, the wise and understanding person may now well calculate that no **dissolution** of the **Bodies** should be, nor happen, except in its own **blood** <note>In alchemy, "blood" is often a metaphor for the "mercurial essence" or the internal "soul" of the metal that allows it to be dissolved and reborn.</note>, and no fruit may be attained unless the **Body** has first been dissolved—a path which you will hereafter clearly undertake.

Take, in the name of the Lord, the very best **Sublimated Mercury**, which has been sublimated seven times, and **revivify** <note>original: "revificir"; to return a chemical substance to its metallic or "living" state</note> it again using one part **Quicklime** <note>original: "lebendig Kalck"; calcium oxide, used here as a caustic purifying agent</note> and half as much by weight of **Crude Tartar** <note>original: "Tartarum crudum"; potassium bitartrate, a sediment from wine casks used as a flux and cleaning agent</note>. In this way, it will be well **purged** <note>purified of impurities</note>, or purge it as best as you are able. Take three parts of this same **Mercury**, and one part of thinly beaten **Gold or Silver**—the kind that **Painters** <note>referring to gold or silver leaf used by artists and illuminators, which, being very thin, dissolves more easily into mercury</note> use—and add it together...

# Preface.

Kind, dear reader, in the conversation between Alberti and Georgi, it is mentioned that the same author wrote another little book containing the **theory** of the birth of **minerals**, (a) and the **preparation of the Physical Stone**; <note>original Latin/German: "Theoricam... ---

(a) This little book was published in the year 1706 by Mr. Johann Zieger, a bookseller in Nuremberg, under the following **title**: **Mineralogy**, or, **Chemical Key**; <note>original: "Mineralogia, oder, Chymischer Schlußel."</note> that is: A brief report on how the nature and properties of all metals and minerals should be most easily explored and investigated: it also points out and demonstrates a near way to reach the **Universal**; <note>The "Universal" refers to the Universal Medicine or the Great Work, the ultimate objective of the alchemist.</note> finally, the circulated riddle: "I am neither creature nor a creator," <term>etc.</term> <note>This specific riddle refers to the "First Matter" (Prima Materia), the chaotic substance from which the Stone is made.</note> is clearly explained in a philosophical manner, presented by **Theophilus**. # The Second Part.

## From which *metals* <note>original: *Metallis*</note> this *composite* <note>original: *Compositum*; the alchemical compound or "Great Work"</note> should proceed into *form* <note>original: *formam*</note> and *matter* <note>original: *materiam*</note>.

Experience teaches that every end must reveal its beginning, as was touched upon above; and it finds that what a thing was in the beginning, it must also be in its *final matter* <note>original: *ultima materia*; the finished state of a substance</note>. This is as the *philosophers* <note>original: *Philosophi*</note> testify: namely, that everything brings forth its own kind, and that no perfect *form* <note>original: *Form*</note> can be *extracted* <note>original: *extrahiret*</note> from any thing, nor led into increase, unless it was previously placed by God in truth into the *greater works* <note>original: *Majora*; likely referring to the higher macrocosmic or divine archetypes</note> and is found *in actual existence* <note>original: *in actu*</note>. 

This is testified to not only by **PHILIPPUS THEOPHRASTUS** <note>referring to the famous alchemist Paracelsus</note>, who says that nothing is so small that is intended to become something which may exist without *form* <note>original: *Form*</note>, but also by the *philosopher* <note>original: *Philosophus*</note> Aristotle and others who shall follow hereafter. They state that nothing can be born or come to be unless the *form* <note>original: *Form*</note> is *joined* <note>original: *copuliret*</note> and added to the *matter* <note>original: *Materiæ*</note>; for these, they say, are the essential *principles* <note>original: *Principia*</note> of every thing that is to be born.

# Metallurgy <note>original: *Metallurgiæ*</note>

Even if **metals** and **gems** <note>original: *Metalla und Gemmas*</note> are improved when they are found to have been **digested** <term>digested: *digeriret*; in alchemy, a process of slow, gentle heating to mature a substance over time</term> within their own proper time, such a thing does not belong to this, our work and **Mastery** <note>original: *Magisterio*; refers to the "Great Work" of alchemy</note>—which is **transmuted** <note>original: *transmutiret*</note> through special labor and a new birth. For if this, our **heavenly Medicine** <note>original: *himmlische Medicin*</note>, is to show its proper power, it must proceed from the **root** and **first Matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note> of all metals, as has been sufficiently shown above; for nature itself proves this, as much in **vegetables** and **animals** as in **minerals** <note>original: *Vegetabilibus, Animalibus, Mineralibus*</note>, as can be understood from the following.

For, as an example, if a tree-fruit or grain is to be brought to **increase** <note>original: *Augmentation*</note>, the seed of the fruit one wishes to multiply must be sown in the earth. Now, the seed cannot take its **nourishment** <note>original: *Nutriment*</note> and increase into itself while in the earth unless it first rots and is **reduced** <note>original: *reduciret*</note> into **first Matter** <term>first matter: *primam Materiam*; the chaotic, undifferentiated state of a substance before it takes a specific form</term> through the moisture of the earth, so that it can unite with the **liquid of the earth** <note>original: *liquore terræ*</note> and feed and water the seed. ...manifestly brought those things to light which previously, and in the old life, were all in potentiality <note>original: *in potentiâ*; existing as a possibility rather than in actuality</note> and invisibly hidden. # Metallurgy
<meta>catchword: .talli- (likely continuing "metallic" or "metallurgy")</meta>

If this fire or sulfur <note>In alchemy, "sulfur" represents the active, masculine, and fiery principle that gives form to "mercury," the passive substrate.</note> is to transform its own matter <note>original: *Materiam*</note> through its power into its own fiery nature and transform it completely <note>original: *simpliciter*</note>, then that same matter must become equal to it in the simplicity of the second unity—that is, in the decad <note>original: *denario*; the number ten, which in Pythagorean philosophy represents a return to unity at a higher level after a full cycle of numbers.</note>—so that through this fire, acting as the form <note>The "form" is the organizing essence or soul that dictates what a substance is, as opposed to its raw material.</note>, it may also penetrate the matter into fire, and particularly into its form and simplicity, and thus reach the second unity and perfection <note>original: *Perfection*</note>. At that point, nothing shall be lacking that is not also truly fire and sulfur. This must be observed in specific individual substances <note>original: *speciebus individuorum*</note> not only in quality, but also in quantity, since no element can leave another, but all are inseparably mixed. This is the cause and the maintenance of the weight, as is experienced and seen in natural effects: namely, that the matter—which is the binary <note>original: *Binarius*; the number two, representing duality, division, or the raw material before it is unified.</note>—proceeds from the form and unity into the other perfection, the ternary <note>original: *Ternarium*; the number three, often seen as the reconciliation of the binary's conflict into a new, stable whole.</note> (which is a child of unity). For **everything in three is perfect** <note>original: *Quia omne trinum perfectum*</note>, yet not before it arises through the fourth order of the four degrees <note>original: *Gradus*; stages of heat or purification</note>, in simplicity and the decad. That is, it must be raised in our work through the constant application of heat, through the four elements and degrees, and brought to the second unity and perfection; then its power is unspeakable, as **HERMES** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of alchemy and author of the *Emerald Tablet*.</note> shows: *Its power is complete if it be turned into earth.* <note>original: *Vis ejus integra est: si versa fuerit in terram*; a famous maxim from the *Emerald Tablet* suggesting that the spiritual "power" must be stabilized or "fixed" in a physical form.</note> Thus

# Metallurgy
<header>Metallurgy</header>

...sulfur and a fixed degree <note>In alchemy, a "degree" refers to a specific stage of intensity or maturation of the substance.</note> that does not yet dominate the mercury <note>original: *Mercurium*; the fluid, passive, and feminine principle of matter.</note> (which, as Trevisanus <note>Bernard of Treviso (1406–1490), a famous alchemist who argued that the "Stone" must be made solely from metallic ingredients.</note> says, perfects and ripens the whole work). Thus, one need only "plant" into it a small amount of the little book <note>original: *Büchleins*; this may refer to a specific concentrated recipe or a metaphorical "seed" of knowledge.</note>, or the sulfur of the Sun <note>original: *sulphuris Solis*; the active principle derived from gold.</note> or the Moon <note>original: *Lunæ*; the active principle derived from silver.</note>, which alone—as the "form" <note>In the Aristotelian sense, the "form" is the organizing soul or essence that gives raw matter its specific identity.</note> of the entire composition—shapes or carves it into its own nature (as previously indicated). Regardless of how much nature has added to the mercury, one cannot go wrong, as can be well observed in the action of the sulfur of the Sun. Thus, only a tenth part of sulfur will be found relative to the body <note>The "body" is the solid metallic material being transformed.</note> and the mercury; therefore, this proportion must be followed. 

All of this is taught in detail by Trevisanus and other philosophers, as well as by nature itself: that a small portion of ferment <note>original: *fermenti*; much like yeast in dough, a "ferment" in alchemy is a small amount of perfected substance that transforms a larger mass of base metal into its own higher nature.</note> dissolves a large mass of dough. Therefore, Trevisanus says: God has created one, ten, 100, 1000, 10,000, 100,000, 1,000,000, and so on. This is also proven by nature, which begins from unity <note>original: *Unität*; the state of being one, representing the primary source or the perfected Stone.</note> and ends and concludes again in that same unity within the work, which requires careful attention. 

For consider, for example, the spirit or sulfur of the Sun: what is it other than a pure, simple fire and heavenly water that exists only within itself in unity? Just like the Sun in the great world <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe at large.</note>, it needs no other thing to sustain its life, but lives solely from the power of God because of its simple unity, which—

...happens, that it reaches the <term>denarius</term><note>Latin: *denario*; the number ten. In alchemical numerology, 1+2+3+4=10. This was seen as a return to unity on a higher level of completion.</note>, then when 1, 2, 3, and 4 are taken together, they make 10. These four numbers are the fulfillment of all numbers, because it always returns to one again, and beyond 10, there is no longer any simple number.

Therefore, after this <term>matter</term><note>original: *Materi*.</note> has been thus prepared, it should be enclosed in a clear glass vessel (which it should only fill by one third), so that nothing can evaporate out. It is then to be processed with the first degree of heat (which should be so hot that one can hold a hand in the ashes and <term>cupel</term><note>original: *Capellen*; here referring to the heating chamber or sand bath of the furnace.</note> without injury), until the <term>blackness</term><note>This is the *nigredo* stage, representing the "death" or decomposition of the substance before its purification.</note> appears along with all kinds of colors, and then begins to move toward the true whiteness again.

For the whole matter depends on this: that one does not rush and burn it, as the <term>Turba</term><note>Referring to the *Turba Philosophorum* (Assembly of the Philosophers), one of the oldest and most famous Latin alchemical texts.</note> commands: "Honor the King and his consort, so that they do not burn and fly away in smoke." For there are two kinds of whiteness; therefore, one must take care not to <term>augment</term><note>To increase the potency or quantity of the alchemical substance.</note> in the first, which is not the true whiteness. Then the fire should be raised and strengthened a little—so strong that one can just barely endure a hand near it. This shall be continued until it is truly white like snow and <term>fixed</term><note>original: *fix*; a substance that is stable and does not evaporate when subjected to heat.</note>; then the Queen is born.

# Part Three.

Afterward, one must strengthen the fire once again until it turns yellow, and then even more until it reaches the perfect, highest redness. Thus is the King crowned with the crown of his kingdom and ascended to a new birth. Then the <term>Tincture</term><note>The final alchemical substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold or healing illnesses.</note> and <term>Red Lion</term><note>A common alchemical symbol for the final, most potent state of the philosopher's stone.</note> are completed, which, as <term>Theophrastus</term><note>Referring to Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), a famous Swiss-German physician and alchemist.</note> says, has emerged from three in one water through the art of <term>Vulcan</term><note>The Roman god of fire; in alchemy, this refers to the mastery of the furnace and heat.</note>. In this way, GOD has created and concluded everything for His eternal honor in the Trinity. <note>original: "Est lapis trinunus, Metallum trinunum, Lignum trinunum"</note> It is a triune stone, a triune metal, a triune wood, and so it is with all others.

The <term>Multiplication</term><note>The process of increasing the quantity and the transmuting power of the philosopher's stone after it has been created.</note> of our <term>Stone</term><note>original: "Lapidis".</note>, as the Philosophers mention in their books, happens in this way—not that one needs much of it, for no particle could be so small that one would not be able to increase it, so that its power and Tincture extend <term>to infinity</term><note>original: "in infinitum".</note>. This happens, however, when one dissolves the Stone and "feeds and waters" it with the same <term>nourishment</term><note>original: "Nutriment"; the base substance or "mercury" from which the stone was originally produced.</note> from which it was made, and encloses it again as before, and cooks it to perfection, all just as it is written above. For as often as such <term>dissolution</term><note>original: "Solutio".</note> and <term>fixation</term><note>original: "Fixatio"; the process of making a volatile substance solid and resistant to fire.</note> occurs, it becomes ten times stronger than before in its quality, power, and quantity. Thus is the aforementioned saying of <term>Bernard of Trevisan</term><note>A 15th-century Italian alchemist (1406–1490) who wrote extensively on the "multiplication" of the stone's power.</note> explained—namely, that GOD created 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000, 1,000,000.
